system.summary: Numerical code of about 1 600 numbers: vocabulary in alphabetical order by segments of variable length, segments permuted ('one and a half part'); I/J and U/V merged; hook = -s, triangle = -ed.

prior_solution.where: Jacob Wagner's interlinear decipherments, printed in PJM-SS 10:464-65, 11, 13 and Rowland, Official Letter Books of W. C. C. Claiborne 3:211-213. The key itself is listed as not found by the editors; no reconstruction found. Nothing in this repository (12 Nov 2026).

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout set the rules (protocol before the calculation). An AI agent transcribed, aligned and built the partial key; no human palaeographer checked.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agent run by Brice Dudout

solution.what: Groups of the three NARA pieces transcribed line by line.
328 words aligned with the printed decipherments; 261 numbers valued (89 sure, 145 probable, 27 doubtful).
One-and-a-half-part code: alphabetical segments of variable length, permuted; 96 % of sure/probable pairs in order within pages of 50 (controls <= 57 %).
Held-out letter of 25 Nov 1806: 22 of 23 testable new groups fall at their alphabetical place.
History of the code from Founders and Rowland: sent 8 July 1805, received 12 Aug 1805; Graham's Weber 419-30 code is Sargent's, a different one.

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: Values read off Wagner's interlinear decipherments of the same letters; structure validated on a held-out letter.

validation.notes: Structure: 22/23 held-out groups at their place; 96 % order in pages of 50 against <= 57 % for controls. Not a validation of a complete key.

outcome.fraction_read_source: The three pieces are aligned word by word with the printed decipherments (328 words); no new reading is claimed.
